entries.title: Ezekiel 32:1
segments: Time and death are mighty levellers.  How do they bring down into the dust the strength and riches and beauty in which men pride themselves. Great and terrible empires, like Assyria, Babylon, and Rome; rich and noble families that have long surrounded themselves with pomp and luxury; renowned warriors, statesmen, and orators; these, with every thing else on which the men of this world set their hearts, sink into the earth together, uncared for and forgotten.  The immortal soul alone, with the deeds which it has done in the body, survives, and goes to God's tribunal, to be rewarded according to its works.

  With thy rivers; rather, "in thy rivers."

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:3

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:5
segments: With thy height; with the mass of thy dead carcass.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:9
segments: Bring thy destruction--into the countries; either the report of Pharaoh's destruction, or the broken fragments of his people.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:10
segments: For thee; in view of my judgments upon thee.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:13
segments: Trouble them; trouble the waters of Egypt by passing through them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:14
segments: Make their waters deep; rather, "settle their waters."  The waters of Egypt, being left without man or beast, shall flow clear and smooth; that is, the land shall be utterly desolated.
Others, however, understand these words as a promise of returning quiet and prosperity to Egypt when by God's chastisements she shall have been made to know that he is the Lord,
.  Compare
and

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:16
segments: The daughters of the nations; that is, the nations themselves. Compare the expressions, "daughter of Jerusalem," "daughter of Babylon," etc.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:17
segments: Of the month; apparently of the twelfth month,
; that is, fourteen days after the preceding prophecy.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:18
segments:
Cast them down; to the pit, that is, declare their casting down in a solemn lamentation. 
 
  Her, and the daughters of the famous nations; in the lamentation, or song, that follows, Pharaoh with his people is represented as going down to the pit, to join the great multitude of princes and warriors that have descended thither before him.  By a bold poetic figure, the spirits of these are represented as gathered in the lower world, while the graves of their bodies stand around them. Compare

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:19
segments: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? in this question God rebukes Egypt for glorying in her superior beauty, and at the same time intimates that this shall not save her from perishing with the other uncircumcised nations.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:20
segments:
They shall fall; the Egyptians. 
 
  Draw her; drag her down to the pit.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:21
segments: Shall speak; in amazement at his fall.  Compare

. 
 
  To him--with them that help him; to Pharoah and his allies. 
 
  They are gone down; "the strong among the nations," whom the prophet afterwards enumerates.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:22
segments: His graves are about him; the spirits of the king of Assyria and his warriors are in the pit, by the graves of their bodies.  See note on

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:23
segments: Caused terror in the land of the living; the prophet contrasts their present weakness with the terror they caused while yet alive.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:24
segments:
Elam; Persia. 
 
  Borne their shame; the shame of being slain and sent down to the pit. 
 
  With them; that is, along with the rest of the nations: they are reduced to a common level with them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:25
segments:
Have set her; have appointed for Elam.

. 
 
  He is put; the king of Elam.

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:26
segments: Meshech, Tubal; see note on

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:27
segments:
They shall not lie--the land of the living; more plainly thus: "They shall not lie with the mighty that are fallen of the uncircumcised, who have gone down to hell with their weapons of war, and they have laid their swords under their heads: but their iniquities shall be upon their bones, because they were the terror of the mighty in the land of the living." 
 
  Shall not lie; Meshech and Tubal shall not lie in their graves honorably buried.  A poetical burial in the lower world has been ascribed to them,

; but here a literal burial on earth is denied them. 
 
  With their weapons of war; there is here a blending of the literal with the figurative.  Because their weapons of war have been deposited with them in their graves, they are figuratively represented as having taken them with them to the lower world, just as their graves are figuratively represented as being there with their souls. 
 
  But their iniquities; the iniquities of Meshech and Tubal. 
 
  Shall be upon their bones; their bones shall be left unburied, as a punishment for their violence in the land of the living.

segments: Shall be comforted; see note on

entries.title: Ezekiel 32:32
segments: I have caused my terror; another reading of the original is, "I have caused his terror," that is, I have permitted Pharaoh to spread terror.
